meaning.en: This śloka presents Lalitā through the names kālarātryādiśaktyaughavṛtā (Surrounded by kAlarAtri and other shaktis), snigdhaudanapriyā (Fond of food offerings containing ghee, oil and other substances containing fats), mahāvīrendravaradā (bestows boons on great warriors), and rākiṇyambāsvarūpiṇī (the form of the rAkiNi deity). The movement of the verse is cumulative: each nāma adds a distinct quality, so the Mother is seen at once through several complementary dimensions rather than through a single isolated attribute.
meaning.kn: ಈ ಶ್ಲೋಕವು ಲಲಿತೆಯನ್ನು kālarātryādiśaktyaughavṛtā, snigdhaudanapriyā, mahāvīrendravaradā, rākiṇyambāsvarūpiṇī ಎಂಬ ನಾಮಗಳ ಮೂಲಕ ಸ್ತುತಿಸುತ್ತದೆ. ಪ್ರತಿಯೊಂದು ನಾಮವೂ ತನ್ನದೇ ನಿರ್ದಿಷ್ಟ ಅರ್ಥವನ್ನು ನೀಡುತ್ತಿದ್ದು, ಅವು ಒಟ್ಟಾಗಿ ಓದಲ್ಪಟ್ಟಾಗ ತಾಯಿಯ ಈ ಭಾಗದ ಸಮಗ್ರ ದೈವಸ್ವರೂಪವನ್ನು ಸ್ಪಷ್ಟಗೊಳಿಸುತ್ತವೆ.

deeper.en:
The deeper movement of this śloka becomes clearer when the names are read together. kālarātryādiśaktyaughavṛtā, snigdhaudanapriyā, mahāvīrendravaradā, and rākiṇyambāsvarūpiṇī do not simply form a list; they trace a relationship between the verse reveals another facet of the Mother’s nature and adds it to the cumulative vision of Lalitā as beauty, power, consciousness and liberation; the body is not excluded from sacred reality; its tissues, nourishment and functions are included within the Goddess’s cosmic order; Her giving arises from fullness, and the deeper gift is whatever moves a being toward wholeness, right direction and liberation. In that relationship, each name explains something the others leave unstated, so the verse becomes a compact theological portrait rather than a sequence of disconnected epithets.

For a devotee, the verse can therefore be contemplated on two levels at once. On the personal level, Lalitā is the Mother who can be approached, praised and loved through these particular qualities. On the deeper Śrīvidyā level, those same qualities point toward one indivisible Śakti whose beauty, authority, knowledge, compassion and transcendence are not separate powers but facets of a single consciousness.
deeper.kn:

meaning.en: This śloka presents Lalitā through the names medoniṣṭhā (resides in the fat in living beings), madhuprītā (Fond of honey and other offerings made with honey), bandhinyādisamanvitā (Accompanied by bandhini and other shaktis), dadhyannāsaktahṛdayā (Particularly fond of offerings made with curd), and kākinīrūpadhāriṇī (the form of kAkinI yoginI). meaning.en: This śloka presents Lalitā through the names puṇyakīrtiḥ (She whose fame is sacred or righteous), puṇyalabhyā (Attained only by righteous souls), puṇyaśravaṇakīrtanā (bestows merit on anyone who hears of Her and praises Her), pulomajārcitā (Worshipped by pulomaja (Indra's wife)), bandhamocanī (Free from bonds; She who gives release from bondage), and barbarālakā (She whose hair forms curly or wavy locks). ಭಕ್ತನಿಗೆ ಈ ಶ್ಲೋಕವನ್ನು ಎರಡು ಮಟ್ಟಗಳಲ್ಲಿ ಧ್ಯಾನಿಸಬಹುದು. ಆಪ್ತಮಟ್ಟದಲ್ಲಿ ಲಲಿತೆ ಈ ವಿಶಿಷ್ಟ ಗುಣಗಳೊಂದಿಗೆ ಪ್ರೀತಿಯಿಂದ ಆರಾಧಿಸಬಹುದಾದ ತಾಯಿ. ಶ್ರೀವಿದ್ಯೆಯ ಆಳವಾದ ಮಟ್ಟದಲ್ಲಿ ಇದೇ ಗುಣಗಳು ಒಂದೇ ಅವಿಭಾಜ್ಯ ಶಕ್ತಿಯ ವಿಭಿನ್ನ ಪ್ರಕಾಶಗಳು—ಸೌಂದರ್ಯ, ಅಧಿಪತ್ಯ, ಜ್ಞಾನ, ಕರುಣೆ ಮತ್ತು ಪರಾತ್ಪರತೆ ಬೇರೆ ಬೇರೆ ಶಕ್ತಿಗಳಲ್ಲ, ಒಂದೇ ಚೈತನ್ಯದ ಮುಖಗಳು.

meaning.en: This śloka presents Lalitā through the names tāmbūlapūritamukhī (She whose mouth is full from chewing betel), dāḍimīkusumaprabhā (shines like a pomegranate flower), mṛgākṣī (She whose eyes are long and beautiful like those of a doe), mohinī (Enchanting), mukhyā (First), mṛḍānī (Wife of mRiDa (Śiva)), and mitrarūpiṇī (Friend of everyone (universe)). The movement of the verse is cumulative: each nāma adds a distinct quality, so the Mother is seen at once through several complementary dimensions rather than through a single isolated attribute.
meaning.kn: ಈ ಶ್ಲೋಕವು ಲಲಿತೆಯನ್ನು tāmbūlapūritamukhī, dāḍimīkusumaprabhā, mṛgākṣī, mohinī, mukhyā, mṛḍānī, mitrarūpiṇī ಎಂಬ ನಾಮಗಳ ಮೂಲಕ ಸ್ತುತಿಸುತ್ತದೆ. ಪ್ರತಿಯೊಂದು ನಾಮವೂ ತನ್ನದೇ ನಿರ್ದಿಷ್ಟ ಅರ್ಥವನ್ನು ನೀಡುತ್ತಿದ್ದು, ಅವು ಒಟ್ಟಾಗಿ ಓದಲ್ಪಟ್ಟಾಗ ತಾಯಿಯ ಈ ಭಾಗದ ಸಮಗ್ರ ದೈವಸ್ವರೂಪವನ್ನು ಸ್ಪಷ್ಟಗೊಳಿಸುತ್ತವೆ.

deeper.en:
The deeper movement of this śloka becomes clearer when the names are read together. tāmbūlapūritamukhī, dāḍimīkusumaprabhā, mṛgākṣī, and mohinī and the remaining nāmas do not simply form a list; they trace a relationship between the verse reveals another facet of the Mother’s nature and adds it to the cumulative vision of Lalitā as beauty, power, consciousness and liberation; the beauty of Her form is used as a devotional doorway that gathers the mind into loving concentration before leading it beyond all finite images; images of sun, moon, fire and radiance point both to devotional beauty and to illumination—the power by which what is hidden becomes known. In that relationship, each name explains something the others leave unstated, so the verse becomes a compact theological portrait rather than a sequence of disconnected epithets.

For a devotee, the verse can therefore be contemplated on two levels at once. On the personal level, Lalitā is the Mother who can be approached, praised and loved through these particular qualities. On the deeper Śrīvidyā level, those same qualities point toward one indivisible Śakti whose beauty, authority, knowledge, compassion and transcendence are not separate powers but facets of a single consciousness.

ಭಕ್ತನಿಗೆ ಈ ಶ್ಲೋಕವನ್ನು ಎರಡು ಮಟ್ಟಗಳಲ್ಲಿ ಧ್ಯಾನಿಸಬಹುದು. ಆಪ್ತಮಟ್ಟದಲ್ಲಿ ಲಲಿತೆ ಈ ವಿಶಿಷ್ಟ ಗುಣಗಳೊಂದಿಗೆ ಪ್ರೀತಿಯಿಂದ ಆರಾಧಿಸಬಹುದಾದ ತಾಯಿ. ಶ್ರೀವಿದ್ಯೆಯ ಆಳವಾದ ಮಟ್ಟದಲ್ಲಿ ಇದೇ ಗುಣಗಳು ಒಂದೇ ಅವಿಭಾಜ್ಯ ಶಕ್ತಿಯ ವಿಭಿನ್ನ ಪ್ರಕಾಶಗಳು—ಸೌಂದರ್ಯ, ಅಧಿಪತ್ಯ, ಜ್ಞಾನ, ಕರುಣೆ ಮತ್ತು ಪರಾತ್ಪರತೆ ಬೇರೆ ಬೇರೆ ಶಕ್ತಿಗಳಲ್ಲ, ಒಂದೇ ಚೈತನ್ಯದ ಮುಖಗಳು.

meaning.en: This śloka presents Lalitā through the names mahākailāsanilayā (resides in the great kailAsa), mṛṇālamṛdudorlatā (She whose arms are as soft and cool as the lotus stem), mahanīyā (Adorable), dayāmūrtiḥ (Personification of compassion), and mahāsāmrājyaśālinī (controls the great empire of the three worlds). The movement of the verse is cumulative: each nāma adds a distinct quality, so the Mother is seen at once through several complementary dimensions rather than through a single isolated attribute.
meaning.kn: ಈ ಶ್ಲೋಕವು ಲಲಿತೆಯನ್ನು mahākailāsanilayā, mṛṇālamṛdudorlatā, mahanīyā, dayāmūrtiḥ, mahāsāmrājyaśālinī ಎಂಬ ನಾಮಗಳ ಮೂಲಕ ಸ್ತುತಿಸುತ್ತದೆ. ಪ್ರತಿಯೊಂದು ನಾಮವೂ ತನ್ನದೇ ನಿರ್ದಿಷ್ಟ ಅರ್ಥವನ್ನು ನೀಡುತ್ತಿದ್ದು, ಅವು ಒಟ್ಟಾಗಿ ಓದಲ್ಪಟ್ಟಾಗ ತಾಯಿಯ ಈ ಭಾಗದ ಸಮಗ್ರ ದೈವಸ್ವರೂಪವನ್ನು ಸ್ಪಷ್ಟಗೊಳಿಸುತ್ತವೆ.

deeper.en:
The deeper movement of this śloka becomes clearer when the names are read together. mahākailāsanilayā, mṛṇālamṛdudorlatā, mahanīyā, and dayāmūrtiḥ and the remaining nāmas do not simply form a list; they trace a relationship between the verse reveals another facet of the Mother’s nature and adds it to the cumulative vision of Lalitā as beauty, power, consciousness and liberation; the beauty of Her form is used as a devotional doorway that gathers the mind into loving concentration before leading it beyond all finite images; the verse emphasizes that the Infinite is not remote; Lalitā responds through compassion, devotion and a direct relationship with the devotee. In that relationship, each name explains something the others leave unstated, so the verse becomes a compact theological portrait rather than a sequence of disconnected epithets.

For a devotee, the verse can therefore be contemplated on two levels at once. On the personal level, Lalitā is the Mother who can be approached, praised and loved through these particular qualities. On the deeper Śrīvidyā level, those same qualities point toward one indivisible Śakti whose beauty, authority, knowledge, compassion and transcendence are not separate powers but facets of a single consciousness.

ಭಕ್ತನಿಗೆ ಈ ಶ್ಲೋಕವನ್ನು ಎರಡು ಮಟ್ಟಗಳಲ್ಲಿ ಧ್ಯಾನಿಸಬಹುದು. ಆಪ್ತಮಟ್ಟದಲ್ಲಿ ಲಲಿತೆ ಈ ವಿಶಿಷ್ಟ ಗುಣಗಳೊಂದಿಗೆ ಪ್ರೀತಿಯಿಂದ ಆರಾಧಿಸಬಹುದಾದ ತಾಯಿ. ಶ್ರೀವಿದ್ಯೆಯ ಆಳವಾದ ಮಟ್ಟದಲ್ಲಿ ಇದೇ ಗುಣಗಳು ಒಂದೇ ಅವಿಭಾಜ್ಯ ಶಕ್ತಿಯ ವಿಭಿನ್ನ ಪ್ರಕಾಶಗಳು—ಸೌಂದರ್ಯ, ಅಧಿಪತ್ಯ, ಜ್ಞಾನ, ಕರುಣೆ ಮತ್ತು ಪರಾತ್ಪರತೆ ಬೇರೆ ಬೇರೆ ಶಕ್ತಿಗಳಲ್ಲ, ಒಂದೇ ಚೈತನ್ಯದ ಮುಖಗಳು.

meaning.en: This śloka presents Lalitā through the names hṛdayasthā (resides in the heart), raviprakhyā (shines with the special brilliance of the sun), trikoṇāntaradīpikā (shines as a light within the triangle), dākṣāyaṇī (SatIdevI, the daughter of dakSha prajApati), daityahantrī (Killer of demons), and dakṣayajñavināśinī (Destroyer of the sacrifice conducted by dakSha). The movement of the verse is cumulative: each nāma adds a distinct quality, so the Mother is seen at once through several complementary dimensions rather than through a single isolated attribute.
meaning.kn: ಈ ಶ್ಲೋಕವು ಲಲಿತೆಯನ್ನು hṛdayasthā, raviprakhyā, trikoṇāntaradīpikā, dākṣāyaṇī, daityahantrī, dakṣayajñavināśinī ಎಂಬ ನಾಮಗಳ ಮೂಲಕ ಸ್ತುತಿಸುತ್ತದೆ. ಪ್ರತಿಯೊಂದು ನಾಮವೂ ತನ್ನದೇ ನಿರ್ದಿಷ್ಟ ಅರ್ಥವನ್ನು ನೀಡುತ್ತಿದ್ದು, ಅವು ಒಟ್ಟಾಗಿ ಓದಲ್ಪಟ್ಟಾಗ ತಾಯಿಯ ಈ ಭಾಗದ ಸಮಗ್ರ ದೈವಸ್ವರೂಪವನ್ನು ಸ್ಪಷ್ಟಗೊಳಿಸುತ್ತವೆ.

deeper.en:
The deeper movement of this śloka becomes clearer when the names are read together. hṛdayasthā, raviprakhyā, trikoṇāntaradīpikā, and dākṣāyaṇī and the remaining nāmas do not simply form a list; they trace a relationship between the verse reveals another facet of the Mother’s nature and adds it to the cumulative vision of Lalitā as beauty, power, consciousness and liberation; images of sun, moon, fire and radiance point both to devotional beauty and to illumination—the power by which what is hidden becomes known; Her fierce aspect is protective rather than arbitrary: what is destroyed is obstruction, ignorance or disorder that prevents dharma and freedom. In that relationship, each name explains something the others leave unstated, so the verse becomes a compact theological portrait rather than a sequence of disconnected epithets.

For a devotee, the verse can therefore be contemplated on two levels at once. On the personal level, Lalitā is the Mother who can be approached, praised and loved through these particular qualities. On the deeper Śrīvidyā level, those same qualities point toward one indivisible Śakti whose beauty, authority, knowledge, compassion and transcendence are not separate powers but facets of a single consciousness.

meaning.en: This śloka presents Lalitā through the names deveśī (Protector of the gods), daṇḍanītisthā (maintains the rules of jusstice without the slightest error), daharākāśarūpiṇī (Subtle self in the heart), and pratipanmukhyarākāntatithimaṇḍalapūjitā (Worshipped daily starting with pratipad (first day of the lunar half-month) and ending with the full moon). ಭಕ್ತನಿಗೆ ಈ ಶ್ಲೋಕವನ್ನು ಎರಡು ಮಟ್ಟಗಳಲ್ಲಿ ಧ್ಯಾನಿಸಬಹುದು. ಆಪ್ತಮಟ್ಟದಲ್ಲಿ ಲಲಿತೆ ಈ ವಿಶಿಷ್ಟ ಗುಣಗಳೊಂದಿಗೆ ಪ್ರೀತಿಯಿಂದ ಆರಾಧಿಸಬಹುದಾದ ತಾಯಿ. ಶ್ರೀವಿದ್ಯೆಯ ಆಳವಾದ ಮಟ್ಟದಲ್ಲಿ ಇದೇ ಗುಣಗಳು ಒಂದೇ ಅವಿಭಾಜ್ಯ ಶಕ್ತಿಯ ವಿಭಿನ್ನ ಪ್ರಕಾಶಗಳು—ಸೌಂದರ್ಯ, ಅಧಿಪತ್ಯ, ಜ್ಞಾನ, ಕರುಣೆ ಮತ್ತು ಪರಾತ್ಪರತೆ ಬೇರೆ ಬೇರೆ ಶಕ್ತಿಗಳಲ್ಲ, ಒಂದೇ ಚೈತನ್ಯದ ಮುಖಗಳು.

meaning.en: This śloka presents Lalitā through the names tryakṣari (She whose form consists of three letters or syllables (Om = a u m)), divyagandhāḍhyā (Richly endowed with divine fragrance), sindūratilakāñcitā (shines witha vermillion mark on Her forehead; She who is decorated with a special paste made of vermilion), umā (PArvatI devI), śailendratanayā (Daughter of himavat, the king of the mountains), gaurī (a fair complexion), and gandharvasevitā (Served by gandharvas (like vishvAvasu)). The movement of the verse is cumulative: each nāma adds a distinct quality, so the Mother is seen at once through several complementary dimensions rather than through a single isolated attribute.
meaning.kn: ಈ ಶ್ಲೋಕವು ಲಲಿತೆಯನ್ನು tryakṣari, divyagandhāḍhyā, sindūratilakāñcitā, umā, śailendratanayā, gaurī, gandharvasevitā ಎಂಬ ನಾಮಗಳ ಮೂಲಕ ಸ್ತುತಿಸುತ್ತದೆ. ಪ್ರತಿಯೊಂದು ನಾಮವೂ ತನ್ನದೇ ನಿರ್ದಿಷ್ಟ ಅರ್ಥವನ್ನು ನೀಡುತ್ತಿದ್ದು, ಅವು ಒಟ್ಟಾಗಿ ಓದಲ್ಪಟ್ಟಾಗ ತಾಯಿಯ ಈ ಭಾಗದ ಸಮಗ್ರ ದೈವಸ್ವರೂಪವನ್ನು ಸ್ಪಷ್ಟಗೊಳಿಸುತ್ತವೆ.

deeper.en:
The deeper movement of this śloka becomes clearer when the names are read together. tryakṣari, divyagandhāḍhyā, sindūratilakāñcitā, and umā and the remaining nāmas do not simply form a list; they trace a relationship between the verse reveals another facet of the Mother’s nature and adds it to the cumulative vision of Lalitā as beauty, power, consciousness and liberation; Her fierce aspect is protective rather than arbitrary: what is destroyed is obstruction, ignorance or disorder that prevents dharma and freedom; Lalitā is not merely knowledgeable but is identified with consciousness and knowing itself, the light in which every act of understanding takes place. In that relationship, each name explains something the others leave unstated, so the verse becomes a compact theological portrait rather than a sequence of disconnected epithets.

For a devotee, the verse can therefore be contemplated on two levels at once. On the personal level, Lalitā is the Mother who can be approached, praised and loved through these particular qualities. On the deeper Śrīvidyā level, those same qualities point toward one indivisible Śakti whose beauty, authority, knowledge, compassion and transcendence are not separate powers but facets of a single consciousness.

meaning.en: This śloka presents Lalitā through the names viśvagarbhā (contains the whole universe in Her womb), svarṇagarbhā (Cause of the universe), avaradā (Destroyer of the unholy), vāgadhīśvarī (presides over speech), dhyānagamyā (To be attained through meditation), aparicchedyā (She whose limits cannot be ascertained (unlimited)), jñānadā (Giver of knowledge of the self), and jñānavigrahā (Sthe embodiment of knowledge itself). ಭಕ್ತನಿಗೆ ಈ ಶ್ಲೋಕವನ್ನು ಎರಡು ಮಟ್ಟಗಳಲ್ಲಿ ಧ್ಯಾನಿಸಬಹುದು. ಆಪ್ತಮಟ್ಟದಲ್ಲಿ ಲಲಿತೆ ಈ ವಿಶಿಷ್ಟ ಗುಣಗಳೊಂದಿಗೆ ಪ್ರೀತಿಯಿಂದ ಆರಾಧಿಸಬಹುದಾದ ತಾಯಿ. ಶ್ರೀವಿದ್ಯೆಯ ಆಳವಾದ ಮಟ್ಟದಲ್ಲಿ ಇದೇ ಗುಣಗಳು ಒಂದೇ ಅವಿಭಾಜ್ಯ ಶಕ್ತಿಯ ವಿಭಿನ್ನ ಪ್ರಕಾಶಗಳು—ಸೌಂದರ್ಯ, ಅಧಿಪತ್ಯ, ಜ್ಞಾನ, ಕರುಣೆ ಮತ್ತು ಪರಾತ್ಪರತೆ ಬೇರೆ ಬೇರೆ ಶಕ್ತಿಗಳಲ್ಲ, ಒಂದೇ ಚೈತನ್ಯದ ಮುಖಗಳು.

meaning.en: This śloka presents Lalitā through the names adṛśyā (Not perceived by sense organs (normal eyes)), dṛśyarahitā (nothing to see), vijñātrī (knows the truth of the physical universe), vedyavarjitā (nothing left to know), yoginī (Constantly united with parAshiva; She who possesses the power of yoga), yogadā (bestows the power of yoga), yogyā (deserves yoga of all kinds), yogānandā (Bliss attained through yoga; She who enjoys the bliss of yoga), and yugandharā (Bearer of the yugas). The movement of the verse is cumulative: each nāma adds a distinct quality, so the Mother is seen at once through several complementary dimensions rather than through a single isolated attribute.
meaning.kn: ಈ ಶ್ಲೋಕವು ಲಲಿತೆಯನ್ನು adṛśyā, dṛśyarahitā, vijñātrī, vedyavarjitā, yoginī, yogadā, yogyā, yogānandā, yugandharā ಎಂಬ ನಾಮಗಳ ಮೂಲಕ ಸ್ತುತಿಸುತ್ತದೆ. ಪ್ರತಿಯೊಂದು ನಾಮವೂ ತನ್ನದೇ ನಿರ್ದಿಷ್ಟ ಅರ್ಥವನ್ನು ನೀಡುತ್ತಿದ್ದು, ಅವು ಒಟ್ಟಾಗಿ ಓದಲ್ಪಟ್ಟಾಗ ತಾಯಿಯ ಈ ಭಾಗದ ಸಮಗ್ರ ದೈವಸ್ವರೂಪವನ್ನು ಸ್ಪಷ್ಟಗೊಳಿಸುತ್ತವೆ.

deeper.en:
The deeper movement of this śloka becomes clearer when the names are read together. adṛśyā, dṛśyarahitā, vijñātrī, and vedyavarjitā and the remaining nāmas do not simply form a list; they trace a relationship between the verse turns inward to the states and centres of consciousness, showing the Goddess as the presence that moves through them and also exceeds them; the verse reveals another facet of the Mother’s nature and adds it to the cumulative vision of Lalitā as beauty, power, consciousness and liberation; the verse expands Lalitā beyond a localized deity-form and identifies Her with the whole field of existence. In that relationship, each name explains something the others leave unstated, so the verse becomes a compact theological portrait rather than a sequence of disconnected epithets.

For a devotee, the verse can therefore be contemplated on two levels at once. On the personal level, Lalitā is the Mother who can be approached, praised and loved through these particular qualities. On the deeper Śrīvidyā level, those same qualities point toward one indivisible Śakti whose beauty, authority, knowledge, compassion and transcendence are not separate powers but facets of a single consciousness.

ಭಕ್ತನಿಗೆ ಈ ಶ್ಲೋಕವನ್ನು ಎರಡು ಮಟ್ಟಗಳಲ್ಲಿ ಧ್ಯಾನಿಸಬಹುದು. ಆಪ್ತಮಟ್ಟದಲ್ಲಿ ಲಲಿತೆ ಈ ವಿಶಿಷ್ಟ ಗುಣಗಳೊಂದಿಗೆ ಪ್ರೀತಿಯಿಂದ ಆರಾಧಿಸಬಹುದಾದ ತಾಯಿ. ಶ್ರೀವಿದ್ಯೆಯ ಆಳವಾದ ಮಟ್ಟದಲ್ಲಿ ಇದೇ ಗುಣಗಳು ಒಂದೇ ಅವಿಭಾಜ್ಯ ಶಕ್ತಿಯ ವಿಭಿನ್ನ ಪ್ರಕಾಶಗಳು—ಸೌಂದರ್ಯ, ಅಧಿಪತ್ಯ, ಜ್ಞಾನ, ಕರುಣೆ ಮತ್ತು ಪರಾತ್ಪರತೆ ಬೇರೆ ಬೇರೆ ಶಕ್ತಿಗಳಲ್ಲ, ಒಂದೇ ಚೈತನ್ಯದ ಮುಖಗಳು.

meaning.en: This śloka presents Lalitā through the names annadā (Giver of food to all living things), vasudā (Giver of wealth), vṛddhā (Ancient), brahmātmaikyasvarūpiṇī (She whose nature is the union of brahman and Atman), bṛhatī (Immense), brāhmaṇī (Predominantly sAttvic), brāhmī (presides over speech), brahmānandā (Ever immersed in the bliss of brahman), and balipriyā (Especially fond of sacrificial offerings). The movement of the verse is cumulative: each nāma adds a distinct quality, so the Mother is seen at once through several complementary dimensions rather than through a single isolated attribute.
meaning.kn: ಈ ಶ್ಲೋಕವು ಲಲಿತೆಯನ್ನು annadā, vasudā, vṛddhā, brahmātmaikyasvarūpiṇī, bṛhatī, brāhmaṇī, brāhmī, brahmānandā, balipriyā ಎಂಬ ನಾಮಗಳ ಮೂಲಕ ಸ್ತುತಿಸುತ್ತದೆ. ಪ್ರತಿಯೊಂದು ನಾಮವೂ ತನ್ನದೇ ನಿರ್ದಿಷ್ಟ ಅರ್ಥವನ್ನು ನೀಡುತ್ತಿದ್ದು, ಅವು ಒಟ್ಟಾಗಿ ಓದಲ್ಪಟ್ಟಾಗ ತಾಯಿಯ ಈ ಭಾಗದ ಸಮಗ್ರ ದೈವಸ್ವರೂಪವನ್ನು ಸ್ಪಷ್ಟಗೊಳಿಸುತ್ತವೆ.

deeper.en:
The deeper movement of this śloka becomes clearer when the names are read together. annadā, vasudā, vṛddhā, and brahmātmaikyasvarūpiṇī and the remaining nāmas do not simply form a list; they trace a relationship between the verse reveals another facet of the Mother’s nature and adds it to the cumulative vision of Lalitā as beauty, power, consciousness and liberation; Her giving arises from fullness, and the deeper gift is whatever moves a being toward wholeness, right direction and liberation; the verse expands Lalitā beyond a localized deity-form and identifies Her with the whole field of existence. In that relationship, each name explains something the others leave unstated, so the verse becomes a compact theological portrait rather than a sequence of disconnected epithets.

For a devotee, the verse can therefore be contemplated on two levels at once. On the personal level, Lalitā is the Mother who can be approached, praised and loved through these particular qualities. On the deeper Śrīvidyā level, those same qualities point toward one indivisible Śakti whose beauty, authority, knowledge, compassion and transcendence are not separate powers but facets of a single consciousness.

ಭಕ್ತನಿಗೆ ಈ ಶ್ಲೋಕವನ್ನು ಎರಡು ಮಟ್ಟಗಳಲ್ಲಿ ಧ್ಯಾನಿಸಬಹುದು. ಆಪ್ತಮಟ್ಟದಲ್ಲಿ ಲಲಿತೆ ಈ ವಿಶಿಷ್ಟ ಗುಣಗಳೊಂದಿಗೆ ಪ್ರೀತಿಯಿಂದ ಆರಾಧಿಸಬಹುದಾದ ತಾಯಿ. ಶ್ರೀವಿದ್ಯೆಯ ಆಳವಾದ ಮಟ್ಟದಲ್ಲಿ ಇದೇ ಗುಣಗಳು ಒಂದೇ ಅವಿಭಾಜ್ಯ ಶಕ್ತಿಯ ವಿಭಿನ್ನ ಪ್ರಕಾಶಗಳು—ಸೌಂದರ್ಯ, ಅಧಿಪತ್ಯ, ಜ್ಞಾನ, ಕರುಣೆ ಮತ್ತು ಪರಾತ್ಪರತೆ ಬೇರೆ ಬೇರೆ ಶಕ್ತಿಗಳಲ್ಲ, ಒಂದೇ ಚೈತನ್ಯದ ಮುಖಗಳು.

meaning.en: This śloka presents Lalitā through the names rājyalakṣmī (embodiment of the prosperity of the world), kośanāthā (Mistress of the treasury), caturaṅgabaleśvarī (commands armies of four types), sāmrājyadāyinī (Bestower of imperial dominion), satyasandhā (Devoted to (or maintains) truth), and sāgaramekhalā (Girdled by the oceans). The movement of the verse is cumulative: each nāma adds a distinct quality, so the Mother is seen at once through several complementary dimensions rather than through a single isolated attribute.
meaning.kn: ಈ ಶ್ಲೋಕವು ಲಲಿತೆಯನ್ನು rājyalakṣmī, kośanāthā, caturaṅgabaleśvarī, sāmrājyadāyinī, satyasandhā, sāgaramekhalā ಎಂಬ ನಾಮಗಳ ಮೂಲಕ ಸ್ತುತಿಸುತ್ತದೆ. ಪ್ರತಿಯೊಂದು ನಾಮವೂ ತನ್ನದೇ ನಿರ್ದಿಷ್ಟ ಅರ್ಥವನ್ನು ನೀಡುತ್ತಿದ್ದು, ಅವು ಒಟ್ಟಾಗಿ ಓದಲ್ಪಟ್ಟಾಗ ತಾಯಿಯ ಈ ಭಾಗದ ಸಮಗ್ರ ದೈವಸ್ವರೂಪವನ್ನು ಸ್ಪಷ್ಟಗೊಳಿಸುತ್ತವೆ.

deeper.en:
The deeper movement of this śloka becomes clearer when the names are read together. rājyalakṣmī, kośanāthā, caturaṅgabaleśvarī, and sāmrājyadāyinī and the remaining nāmas do not simply form a list; they trace a relationship between Her giving arises from fullness, and the deeper gift is whatever moves a being toward wholeness, right direction and liberation; royal language expresses spiritual sovereignty: every legitimate power and cosmic function ultimately rests within Her conscious rule; the verse reveals another facet of the Mother’s nature and adds it to the cumulative vision of Lalitā as beauty, power, consciousness and liberation. In that relationship, each name explains something the others leave unstated, so the verse becomes a compact theological portrait rather than a sequence of disconnected epithets.

For a devotee, the verse can therefore be contemplated on two levels at once. On the personal level, Lalitā is the Mother who can be approached, praised and loved through these particular qualities. On the deeper Śrīvidyā level, those same qualities point toward one indivisible Śakti whose beauty, authority, knowledge, compassion and transcendence are not separate powers but facets of a single consciousness.

ಭಕ್ತನಿಗೆ ಈ ಶ್ಲೋಕವನ್ನು ಎರಡು ಮಟ್ಟಗಳಲ್ಲಿ ಧ್ಯಾನಿಸಬಹುದು. ಆಪ್ತಮಟ್ಟದಲ್ಲಿ ಲಲಿತೆ ಈ ವಿಶಿಷ್ಟ ಗುಣಗಳೊಂದಿಗೆ ಪ್ರೀತಿಯಿಂದ ಆರಾಧಿಸಬಹುದಾದ ತಾಯಿ. ಶ್ರೀವಿದ್ಯೆಯ ಆಳವಾದ ಮಟ್ಟದಲ್ಲಿ ಇದೇ ಗುಣಗಳು ಒಂದೇ ಅವಿಭಾಜ್ಯ ಶಕ್ತಿಯ ವಿಭಿನ್ನ ಪ್ರಕಾಶಗಳು—ಸೌಂದರ್ಯ, ಅಧಿಪತ್ಯ, ಜ್ಞಾನ, ಕರುಣೆ ಮತ್ತು ಪರಾತ್ಪರತೆ ಬೇರೆ ಬೇರೆ ಶಕ್ತಿಗಳಲ್ಲ, ಒಂದೇ ಚೈತನ್ಯದ ಮುಖಗಳು.

meaning.en: This śloka presents Lalitā through the names sarvopādhivinirmuktā (Free from all limitations), sadāśivapativratā (SadAshiva's devoted wife), sampradāyeśvarī (Guardian of sacred traditions), sādhu (possesses equanimity), ī (Symbol 'I' (Other versions show 711/712 as sAdhvI eventhough it is a repetition.)), and gurūmaṇḍalarūpiṇī (embodies in Herself the lineage of Gurus). The movement of the verse is cumulative: each nāma adds a distinct quality, so the Mother is seen at once through several complementary dimensions rather than through a single isolated attribute.
meaning.kn: ಈ ಶ್ಲೋಕವು ಲಲಿತೆಯನ್ನು sarvopādhivinirmuktā, sadāśivapativratā, sampradāyeśvarī, sādhu, ī, gurūmaṇḍalarūpiṇī ಎಂಬ ನಾಮಗಳ ಮೂಲಕ ಸ್ತುತಿಸುತ್ತದೆ. ಪ್ರತಿಯೊಂದು ನಾಮವೂ ತನ್ನದೇ ನಿರ್ದಿಷ್ಟ ಅರ್ಥವನ್ನು ನೀಡುತ್ತಿದ್ದು, ಅವು ಒಟ್ಟಾಗಿ ಓದಲ್ಪಟ್ಟಾಗ ತಾಯಿಯ ಈ ಭಾಗದ ಸಮಗ್ರ ದೈವಸ್ವರೂಪವನ್ನು ಸ್ಪಷ್ಟಗೊಳಿಸುತ್ತವೆ.

deeper.en:
The deeper movement of this śloka becomes clearer when the names are read together. sarvopādhivinirmuktā, sadāśivapativratā, sampradāyeśvarī, and sādhu and the remaining nāmas do not simply form a list; they trace a relationship between the verse reveals another facet of the Mother’s nature and adds it to the cumulative vision of Lalitā as beauty, power, consciousness and liberation; the verse removes limitations one by one, reminding us that although She appears in form, Her absolute nature cannot be confined by any category; the verse expands Lalitā beyond a localized deity-form and identifies Her with the whole field of existence. In that relationship, each name explains something the others leave unstated, so the verse becomes a compact theological portrait rather than a sequence of disconnected epithets.

For a devotee, the verse can therefore be contemplated on two levels at once. On the personal level, Lalitā is the Mother who can be approached, praised and loved through these particular qualities. On the deeper Śrīvidyā level, those same qualities point toward one indivisible Śakti whose beauty, authority, knowledge, compassion and transcendence are not separate powers but facets of a single consciousness.

meaning.en: This śloka presents Lalitā through the names kulottīrṇā (transcends the senses), bhagārādhyā (Worshipped in the sun's disc), māyā (Illusion), madhumatī (She whose nature is as sweet as honey), mahī (Goddess earth), gaṇāmbā (Mother of Śiva's attendants), guhyakārādhyā (Worshipped by guhyakas (a kind of devAs)), komalāṅgī (beautiful limbs), and gurupriyā (Beloved of the gurus). ಭಕ್ತನಿಗೆ ಈ ಶ್ಲೋಕವನ್ನು ಎರಡು ಮಟ್ಟಗಳಲ್ಲಿ ಧ್ಯಾನಿಸಬಹುದು. ಆಪ್ತಮಟ್ಟದಲ್ಲಿ ಲಲಿತೆ ಈ ವಿಶಿಷ್ಟ ಗುಣಗಳೊಂದಿಗೆ ಪ್ರೀತಿಯಿಂದ ಆರಾಧಿಸಬಹುದಾದ ತಾಯಿ. ಶ್ರೀವಿದ್ಯೆಯ ಆಳವಾದ ಮಟ್ಟದಲ್ಲಿ ಇದೇ ಗುಣಗಳು ಒಂದೇ ಅವಿಭಾಜ್ಯ ಶಕ್ತಿಯ ವಿಭಿನ್ನ ಪ್ರಕಾಶಗಳು—ಸೌಂದರ್ಯ, ಅಧಿಪತ್ಯ, ಜ್ಞಾನ, ಕರುಣೆ ಮತ್ತು ಪರಾತ್ಪರತೆ ಬೇರೆ ಬೇರೆ ಶಕ್ತಿಗಳಲ್ಲ, ಒಂದೇ ಚೈತನ್ಯದ ಮುಖಗಳು.

meaning.en: This śloka presents Lalitā through the names citkalā (Consciousness in brahman), ānandakalikā (Bud of bliss), premarūpā (Pure love), priyaṅkarī (Bestower of what is dear to Her devotees), nāmapārāyaṇaprītā (Pleased by the repetition of Her names), nandividyā (Deity worshipped by the nandi mantra), and naṭeśvarī (Wife of natesha (Śiva)). The movement of the verse is cumulative: each nāma adds a distinct quality, so the Mother is seen at once through several complementary dimensions rather than through a single isolated attribute.
meaning.kn: ಈ ಶ್ಲೋಕವು ಲಲಿತೆಯನ್ನು citkalā, ānandakalikā, premarūpā, priyaṅkarī, nāmapārāyaṇaprītā, nandividyā, naṭeśvarī ಎಂಬ ನಾಮಗಳ ಮೂಲಕ ಸ್ತುತಿಸುತ್ತದೆ. ಪ್ರತಿಯೊಂದು ನಾಮವೂ ತನ್ನದೇ ನಿರ್ದಿಷ್ಟ ಅರ್ಥವನ್ನು ನೀಡುತ್ತಿದ್ದು, ಅವು ಒಟ್ಟಾಗಿ ಓದಲ್ಪಟ್ಟಾಗ ತಾಯಿಯ ಈ ಭಾಗದ ಸಮಗ್ರ ದೈವಸ್ವರೂಪವನ್ನು ಸ್ಪಷ್ಟಗೊಳಿಸುತ್ತವೆ.

deeper.en:
The deeper movement of this śloka becomes clearer when the names are read together. citkalā, ānandakalikā, premarūpā, and priyaṅkarī and the remaining nāmas do not simply form a list; they trace a relationship between the verse emphasizes that the Infinite is not remote; Lalitā responds through compassion, devotion and a direct relationship with the devotee; Lalitā is not merely knowledgeable but is identified with consciousness and knowing itself, the light in which every act of understanding takes place; the bliss described is not passing pleasure but the fullness that arises when consciousness rests in its own nature. In that relationship, each name explains something the others leave unstated, so the verse becomes a compact theological portrait rather than a sequence of disconnected epithets.

For a devotee, the verse can therefore be contemplated on two levels at once. On the personal level, Lalitā is the Mother who can be approached, praised and loved through these particular qualities. On the deeper Śrīvidyā level, those same qualities point toward one indivisible Śakti whose beauty, authority, knowledge, compassion and transcendence are not separate powers but facets of a single consciousness.

ಭಕ್ತನಿಗೆ ಈ ಶ್ಲೋಕವನ್ನು ಎರಡು ಮಟ್ಟಗಳಲ್ಲಿ ಧ್ಯಾನಿಸಬಹುದು. ಆಪ್ತಮಟ್ಟದಲ್ಲಿ ಲಲಿತೆ ಈ ವಿಶಿಷ್ಟ ಗುಣಗಳೊಂದಿಗೆ ಪ್ರೀತಿಯಿಂದ ಆರಾಧಿಸಬಹುದಾದ ತಾಯಿ. ಶ್ರೀವಿದ್ಯೆಯ ಆಳವಾದ ಮಟ್ಟದಲ್ಲಿ ಇದೇ ಗುಣಗಳು ಒಂದೇ ಅವಿಭಾಜ್ಯ ಶಕ್ತಿಯ ವಿಭಿನ್ನ ಪ್ರಕಾಶಗಳು—ಸೌಂದರ್ಯ, ಅಧಿಪತ್ಯ, ಜ್ಞಾನ, ಕರುಣೆ ಮತ್ತು ಪರಾತ್ಪರತೆ ಬೇರೆ ಬೇರೆ ಶಕ್ತಿಗಳಲ್ಲ, ಒಂದೇ ಚೈತನ್ಯದ ಮುಖಗಳು.

meaning.en: This śloka presents Lalitā through the names bhaktacittakekighanāghanā (Cloud that gladdens the peacocks who are the hearts of Her devotees), rogaparvatadambholiḥ (Thunderbolt that shatters the mountain of disease), and mṛtyudārukuṭhārikā (Axe that cuts down the tree of death). Together they form a concentrated statement about who the Mother is in this portion of the Sahasranāma, allowing each name to deepen the meaning of the others.
meaning.kn: ಈ ಶ್ಲೋಕವು ಲಲಿತೆಯನ್ನು bhaktacittakekighanāghanā, rogaparvatadambholiḥ, mṛtyudārukuṭhārikā ಎಂಬ ನಾಮಗಳ ಮೂಲಕ ಸ್ತುತಿಸುತ್ತದೆ. ಪ್ರತಿಯೊಂದು ನಾಮವೂ ತನ್ನದೇ ನಿರ್ದಿಷ್ಟ ಅರ್ಥವನ್ನು ನೀಡುತ್ತಿದ್ದು, ಅವು ಒಟ್ಟಾಗಿ ಓದಲ್ಪಟ್ಟಾಗ ತಾಯಿಯ ಈ ಭಾಗದ ಸಮಗ್ರ ದೈವಸ್ವರೂಪವನ್ನು ಸ್ಪಷ್ಟಗೊಳಿಸುತ್ತವೆ.

deeper.en:
The deeper movement of this śloka becomes clearer when the names are read together. bhaktacittakekighanāghanā, rogaparvatadambholiḥ, and mṛtyudārukuṭhārikā do not simply form a list; they trace a relationship between the verse emphasizes that the Infinite is not remote; Lalitā responds through compassion, devotion and a direct relationship with the devotee; Lalitā is not merely knowledgeable but is identified with consciousness and knowing itself, the light in which every act of understanding takes place; the verse reveals another facet of the Mother’s nature and adds it to the cumulative vision of Lalitā as beauty, power, consciousness and liberation. In that relationship, each name explains something the others leave unstated, so the verse becomes a compact theological portrait rather than a sequence of disconnected epithets.

For a devotee, the verse can therefore be contemplated on two levels at once. On the personal level, Lalitā is the Mother who can be approached, praised and loved through these particular qualities. On the deeper Śrīvidyā level, those same qualities point toward one indivisible Śakti whose beauty, authority, knowledge, compassion and transcendence are not separate powers but facets of a single consciousness.

meaning.en: This śloka presents Lalitā through the names maheśvarī (Supreme goddess), mahākālī (Great kAli), mahāgrāsā (devours everything great; She who is the great devourer), mahāśanā (eats everything that is great), aparṇā (owes no debt), caṇḍikā (Angry (at the wicked)), and caṇḍamuṇḍāsuraniṣūdinī (killed chaNDa, muNDa and other asuras). ಭಕ್ತನಿಗೆ ಈ ಶ್ಲೋಕವನ್ನು ಎರಡು ಮಟ್ಟಗಳಲ್ಲಿ ಧ್ಯಾನಿಸಬಹುದು. ಆಪ್ತಮಟ್ಟದಲ್ಲಿ ಲಲಿತೆ ಈ ವಿಶಿಷ್ಟ ಗುಣಗಳೊಂದಿಗೆ ಪ್ರೀತಿಯಿಂದ ಆರಾಧಿಸಬಹುದಾದ ತಾಯಿ. ಶ್ರೀವಿದ್ಯೆಯ ಆಳವಾದ ಮಟ್ಟದಲ್ಲಿ ಇದೇ ಗುಣಗಳು ಒಂದೇ ಅವಿಭಾಜ್ಯ ಶಕ್ತಿಯ ವಿಭಿನ್ನ ಪ್ರಕಾಶಗಳು—ಸೌಂದರ್ಯ, ಅಧಿಪತ್ಯ, ಜ್ಞಾನ, ಕರುಣೆ ಮತ್ತು ಪರಾತ್ಪರತೆ ಬೇರೆ ಬೇರೆ ಶಕ್ತಿಗಳಲ್ಲ, ಒಂದೇ ಚೈತನ್ಯದ ಮುಖಗಳು.

meaning.en: This śloka presents Lalitā through the names svargāpavargadā (bestows heaven and liberation), śuddhā (Purest), japāpuṣpanibhākṛtiḥ (She whose body is like the hibiscus flower), ojovatī (Full of vitality), dyutidharā (Full of light and splendor; She who has an aura of light), yajñarūpā (the form of sacrifice), and priyavratā (Fond of vows). The movement of the verse is cumulative: each nāma adds a distinct quality, so the Mother is seen at once through several complementary dimensions rather than through a single isolated attribute.
meaning.kn: ಈ ಶ್ಲೋಕವು ಲಲಿತೆಯನ್ನು svargāpavargadā, śuddhā, japāpuṣpanibhākṛtiḥ, ojovatī, dyutidharā, yajñarūpā, priyavratā ಎಂಬ ನಾಮಗಳ ಮೂಲಕ ಸ್ತುತಿಸುತ್ತದೆ. ಪ್ರತಿಯೊಂದು ನಾಮವೂ ತನ್ನದೇ ನಿರ್ದಿಷ್ಟ ಅರ್ಥವನ್ನು ನೀಡುತ್ತಿದ್ದು, ಅವು ಒಟ್ಟಾಗಿ ಓದಲ್ಪಟ್ಟಾಗ ತಾಯಿಯ ಈ ಭಾಗದ ಸಮಗ್ರ ದೈವಸ್ವರೂಪವನ್ನು ಸ್ಪಷ್ಟಗೊಳಿಸುತ್ತವೆ.

deeper.en:
The deeper movement of this śloka becomes clearer when the names are read together. svargāpavargadā, śuddhā, japāpuṣpanibhākṛtiḥ, and ojovatī and the remaining nāmas do not simply form a list; they trace a relationship between the verse reveals another facet of the Mother’s nature and adds it to the cumulative vision of Lalitā as beauty, power, consciousness and liberation; the bliss described is not passing pleasure but the fullness that arises when consciousness rests in its own nature; Her giving arises from fullness, and the deeper gift is whatever moves a being toward wholeness, right direction and liberation. In that relationship, each name explains something the others leave unstated, so the verse becomes a compact theological portrait rather than a sequence of disconnected epithets.

For a devotee, the verse can therefore be contemplated on two levels at once. On the personal level, Lalitā is the Mother who can be approached, praised and loved through these particular qualities. On the deeper Śrīvidyā level, those same qualities point toward one indivisible Śakti whose beauty, authority, knowledge, compassion and transcendence are not separate powers but facets of a single consciousness.

ಈ ಶ್ಲೋಕದ ಆಳವಾದ ಅರ್ಥ vīrārādhyā, virāḍrūpā, virajā, and viśvatomukhī ಮತ್ತು ಉಳಿದ ನಾಮಗಳು ಪರಸ್ಪರ ಹೇಗೆ ಸಂಬಂಧಿಸುತ್ತವೆ ಎಂಬುದರಲ್ಲಿ ಇದೆ. ಅವು ಕೇವಲ ಪಟ್ಟಿಯಲ್ಲ; ಈ ಶ್ಲೋಕವು ಲಲಿತೆಯ ಮತ್ತೊಂದು ವಿಶಿಷ್ಟ ಮುಖವನ್ನು ಬಿಚ್ಚಿಟ್ಟು, ಸೌಂದರ್ಯ, ಶಕ್ತಿ, ಚೈತನ್ಯ ಮತ್ತು ಮುಕ್ತಿಯ ಸಮಗ್ರ ದೃಷ್ಟಿಯನ್ನು ಗಾಢಗೊಳಿಸುತ್ತದೆ; ಈ ಶ್ಲೋಕವು ದೇವಿಯ ಮೇಲಿನ ಮಿತಿಗಳನ್ನು ಒಂದೊಂದಾಗಿ ತೆಗೆದುಹಾಕುತ್ತದೆ; ಅವಳು ರೂಪದಲ್ಲಿ ಪ್ರಕಟವಾದರೂ ಯಾವುದೇ ವರ್ಗ ಅಥವಾ ಗಡಿಗೂ ಸೀಮಿತಳಲ್ಲ; ದೈವಕೃಪೆಯನ್ನು ಧರ್ಮ, ಕರ್ಮಫಲ ಮತ್ತು ಪವಿತ್ರಕ್ರಮದೊಂದಿಗೆ ಜೋಡಿಸಿ, ಸಮ್ಯಕ ಜೀವನವೂ ಅವಳ ಅಧಿಪತ್ಯದ ಭಾಗವೆಂದು ತೋರಿಸುತ್ತದೆ ಎಂಬ ದೈವಆಯಾಮಗಳನ್ನು ಒಂದೇ ಪ್ರವಾಹದಲ್ಲಿ ಜೋಡಿಸುತ್ತವೆ. ಹೀಗಾಗಿ ಪ್ರತಿಯೊಂದು ನಾಮವೂ ಉಳಿದ ನಾಮಗಳ ಅರ್ಥವನ್ನು ಮತ್ತಷ್ಟು ಗಾಢಗೊಳಿಸುತ್ತದೆ.

ಭಕ್ತನಿಗೆ ಈ ಶ್ಲೋಕವನ್ನು ಎರಡು ಮಟ್ಟಗಳಲ್ಲಿ ಧ್ಯಾನಿಸಬಹುದು. ಆಪ್ತಮಟ್ಟದಲ್ಲಿ ಲಲಿತೆ ಈ ವಿಶಿಷ್ಟ ಗುಣಗಳೊಂದಿಗೆ ಪ್ರೀತಿಯಿಂದ ಆರಾಧಿಸಬಹುದಾದ ತಾಯಿ. ಶ್ರೀವಿದ್ಯೆಯ ಆಳವಾದ ಮಟ್ಟದಲ್ಲಿ ಇದೇ ಗುಣಗಳು ಒಂದೇ ಅವಿಭಾಜ್ಯ ಶಕ್ತಿಯ ವಿಭಿನ್ನ ಪ್ರಕಾಶಗಳು—ಸೌಂದರ್ಯ, ಅಧಿಪತ್ಯ, ಜ್ಞಾನ, ಕರುಣೆ ಮತ್ತು ಪರಾತ್ಪರತೆ ಬೇರೆ ಬೇರೆ ಶಕ್ತಿಗಳಲ್ಲ, ಒಂದೇ ಚೈತನ್ಯದ ಮುಖಗಳು.

meaning.en: This śloka presents Lalitā through the names mārtāṇḍabhairavārādhyā (Worshipped by mArtANDabhairava), mantriṇīnyastarājyadhūḥ (entrusted Her regal responsibilities to Her mantriNi), tripureśī (Goddess of tripura), jayatsenā (an army which is accustomed only to victory), nistraiguṇyā (Devoid of the three guNas), and parāparā (Both parA and aparA). The movement of the verse is cumulative: each nāma adds a distinct quality, so the Mother is seen at once through several complementary dimensions rather than through a single isolated attribute.
meaning.kn: ಈ ಶ್ಲೋಕವು ಲಲಿತೆಯನ್ನು mārtāṇḍabhairavārādhyā, mantriṇīnyastarājyadhūḥ, tripureśī, jayatsenā, nistraiguṇyā, parāparā ಎಂಬ ನಾಮಗಳ ಮೂಲಕ ಸ್ತುತಿಸುತ್ತದೆ. ಪ್ರತಿಯೊಂದು ನಾಮವೂ ತನ್ನದೇ ನಿರ್ದಿಷ್ಟ ಅರ್ಥವನ್ನು ನೀಡುತ್ತಿದ್ದು, ಅವು ಒಟ್ಟಾಗಿ ಓದಲ್ಪಟ್ಟಾಗ ತಾಯಿಯ ಈ ಭಾಗದ ಸಮಗ್ರ ದೈವಸ್ವರೂಪವನ್ನು ಸ್ಪಷ್ಟಗೊಳಿಸುತ್ತವೆ.

deeper.en:
The deeper movement of this śloka becomes clearer when the names are read together. mārtāṇḍabhairavārādhyā, mantriṇīnyastarājyadhūḥ, tripureśī, and jayatsenā and the remaining nāmas do not simply form a list; they trace a relationship between the verse reveals another facet of the Mother’s nature and adds it to the cumulative vision of Lalitā as beauty, power, consciousness and liberation; Śiva and Śakti are presented as inseparable; consciousness and its power of manifestation are two ways of speaking about one Reality; the beauty of Her form is used as a devotional doorway that gathers the mind into loving concentration before leading it beyond all finite images. In that relationship, each name explains something the others leave unstated, so the verse becomes a compact theological portrait rather than a sequence of disconnected epithets.

For a devotee, the verse can therefore be contemplated on two levels at once. On the personal level, Lalitā is the Mother who can be approached, praised and loved through these particular qualities. On the deeper Śrīvidyā level, those same qualities point toward one indivisible Śakti whose beauty, authority, knowledge, compassion and transcendence are not separate powers but facets of a single consciousness.
